core_memory.diabetes_medication_metformin: Metformin 1000 mg twice daily(taken for several years). Helps control blood sugar, but A1C remains around 6.9%.
core_memory.hypothyroidism_medication_levothyroxine: Levothyroxine 75 mcg once daily, taken on an empty stomach, with at least 30 minutes before eating. Last TSH test: 2.1 mIU/L(within normal range). No dosage changes needed.
core_memory.hypothyroidism_dose_mismanagement: Feel sluggish the next day if a dose is missed. Using a pill organizer to stay on track.
core_memory.vitamin_d_intake: Vitamin D3 2,000 IU daily, started after blood test showed low levels(22 ng/mL; normal >30 ng/mL).
core_memory.cholesterol_statin_atorvastatin: Atorvastatin 10 mg daily. Started due to LDL of 130 mg/dL and triglycerides of 140 mg/dL. Cholesterol levels have improved, and no side effects reported(e.g., muscle aches).
core_memory.medication_interactions_kidney_risk: NSAIDs(like meloxicam) can affect kidney function, especially when combined with losartan(an ACE inhibitor). Doctor advised limiting meloxicam use to avoid potential kidney strain. I take it only as needed during flare-ups.
core_memory.medication_interactions_thyroid_absorpti: Take levothyroxine separately from calcium and iron supplements to prevent interference with absorption. Levothyroxine should be taken on an empty stomach, at least 30–60 minutes before meals, and ideally 4–6 hours apart from other medications.
